Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-07-27 16:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (VantageGrid Head of Platform), Jenna Li (Security Lead), Omar Farouk (DevOps)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'm Alex from Redwood, AE on the account, with Priya our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Marco Ruiz: Good, thanks. We wanted to get into the details, we've seen the docs but need to understand the on-prem/vpc split and compliance controls.
[00:12] Priya Patel: Cool. Quick agenda: clarify topology options (hosted, dedicated, private vpc, onprem), security integrations (kms, sso, audit logs), and pilot scope for performance and cost. then next steps. Sound OK?
[00:22] Jenna Li: Yep. Security's primary — SOC2/ISO proof, key management, and the ability to have customer-managed KMS/HSM. Also data residency and audit logs retention windows.
[00:30] Alex Chen: Totally. Redwood supports hosted API, dedicated reserved capacity, and private deployments — with private we can do customer-managed KMS, and there are onprem packages for air-gapped setups. I'll warn that onprem has longer lead times.
[00:42] Omar Farouk: When you say private, do you mean a private control plane inside our VPC or full onprem? we prefer VPC first but might require onprem for certain customers.
[00:49] Priya Patel: Right — we usually offer two private modes: VPC-hosted private control plane where our control plane talks to your workers via peered network, and fully onprem where the control plane is run locally. We can also do a hybrid where control plane is in your cloud region and the runtime is on-prem or in your colo. There are tradeoffs — ops, upgrades, and latency.
[01:08] Marco Ruiz: For latency-sensitive inference we need low tail latency under 40ms p50 for our chat assistants at 256 tokens. Can Redwood hit that in VPC with multi-A100 pools?
[01:18] Priya Patel: Short answer: yes, we've seen p50 in the 20–30ms range for trimmed models on A100 with optimized kernels and continuous batching disabled for low latency paths. caveat: that depends on model size, quantization, and whether caching is enabled. also sequence length profile matters.
[01:32] Jenna Li: What's the KV cache/redis requirement? We have strict firewalling, so we'd need to host caches inside the VPC.
[01:39] Priya Patel: We can place KV caches in your VPC — our runtime supports local prefix caching and can be configured to use your redis or memcached. that requires a private subnet and a couple open ports, we'll document exact rules.
[01:51] Omar Farouk: And what about encryption — at rest and in transit? our security policy mandates TLS between all components and CMK-based at-rest keys.
[01:58] Alex Chen: We support TLS end-to-end; for at-rest, private deployments can use customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, GCP KMS, or an HSM). For hosted accounts we offer envelope encryption, but not customer KMS for lower tiers.
[02:13] Marco Ruiz: Ok. Cost question — dedicated reserved vs private VPC — how should we think about unit economics?
[02:18] Priya Patel: Dedicated reserved gives predictable throughput pricing and lower ops overhead; private VPC/onprem gives full control but can increase ops cost. Redwood Optimize can suggest batching/quantization profiles to reduce per-token cost. For pilot we usually run a benchmark to show cost/latency for typical traffic.
[02:33] Jenna Li: On compliance, can we get SOC2 type II report and any penetration test reports? we need them for procurement.
[02:39] Alex Chen: Yes, i'll send our SOC2/ISO27k artifacts and pen test summary. we'll redact any customer data. expect to receive a secure link.
[02:46] Omar Farouk: Network wise, are there fixed egress IPs we need to whitelist or do you support peering?
[02:51] Priya Patel: We support VPC peering and private link. for hosted fallback we use egress IP ranges but in private setups peering is better. we'll provide a firewall rule sheet.
[03:03] Marco Ruiz: For the pilot we want to validate two things: 1) 72-hour steady-state throughput with our traffic shape, 2) a stress window to simulate bursts. what's a typical pilot footprint?
[03:14] Priya Patel: Typically we propose a small dedicated pool (2–4 GPUs, A100 or equivalent), run a 72-hour benchmark with KV cache enabled and batching tuned, and a 2-hour burst test. we'll collect p50/p95/p99 latency and token cost.
[03:26] Jenna Li: Also need to verify we can rotate keys via our KMS and that audit logs show key usage events.
[03:32] Alex Chen: Good call — we can capture KMS calls and integrate with your CloudTrail/Sentinel logs. We'll outline the integration steps.
[03:39] Omar Farouk: Any blockers on running model quantization or do you require model surgery? we use some open models in fp16 but would prefer int8 for cost.
[03:46] Priya Patel: Redwood runtime supports quantized variants; sometimes we create a quantized build for the model we serve. need to validate quality regressions. Redwood Optimize includes regression checks against your eval set. For open models it's usually straightforward; for proprietary models we do a compat pass.
transcript_continued:
[03:59] Marco Ruiz: There might be regulatory customers that need data never leave country. can you do regionally pinned private deployments?
[04:06] Priya Patel: Yes — we can pin runtime to a region or to a specific onprem cluster. for strict data residency you likely need onprem or a local region private deployment.
[04:14] Jenna Li: What about SSO/SAML and RBAC?
[04:17] Alex Chen: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning and fine-grained RBAC in the console. for private installs we can integrate with your IdP via the same SAML endpoints.
[04:26] Omar Farouk: Are there any non-starter integration pieces? for example we use a locked-down subnet with no outbound internet.
[04:31] Priya Patel: For fully air-gapped networks we offer an onprem appliance but upgrades and telemetry are manual. that increases project timeline and requires our engineering team onsite for initial setup unless you run the installer.
[04:44] Marco Ruiz: Timeline question — if we scope a pilot in August, what does lead time look like for a VPC private sandbox?
[04:49] Alex Chen: For VPC private sandbox typically 2–3 weeks for onboarding (network setup, KMS, firewall), for onprem it's 6–10 weeks depending on procurement and site prep.
[04:59] Priya Patel: We'll also need a sandbox account and a naming and secrets plan. i'll send a checklist.
[05:06] Marco Ruiz: Any RTO/SLA guarantees for Dedicated vs Private?
[05:10] Alex Chen: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets as part of reserved contracts. private SLA can be negotiated; for onprem it's usually best effort unless part of an enterprise support tier.
[05:20] Jenna Li: Procurement will push for indemnities and data processing addendum. is Redwood open to standard DPAs and some clause edits?
[05:26] Alex Chen: We have standard DPA language and enterprise legal can review redlines. For larger customers we do carve-outs in enterprise contracts but it's negotiable.
[05:35] Omar Farouk: Ok that helps. can you share the pilot pricing spreadsheet now or after the call?
[05:39] Alex Chen: i'll attach the pilot pricing and the reserved capacity flavors after the call.
[05:43] Priya Patel: and i'll attach the benchmark template and the firewall checklist.
[05:48] Marco Ruiz: Great. let's talk about metrics we need from the run — we want p50/p95/p99, token/sec, errors per minute, and cost per 1M tokens.
[05:57] Priya Patel: we'll capture those, plus model output quality checks against your eval prompts and a regression alert if quality drops beyond the threshold.
[06:07] Jenna Li: One final sec, on KMS — can you support HSM-backed keys? we use internal HSM for certain customers.
[06:13] Alex Chen: yes, we can integrate with external HSMs for private deployments. that requires a network path to the KMS/HSM or an onprem HSM.
[06:20] Marco Ruiz: OK, let's wrap — recap and owners?
[06:24] Alex Chen: recapping: Alex to send SOC2/ISO and pricing, Priya to send benchmark plan and firewall checklist, Marco to provide sample traffic and sandbox access, Jenna to confirm KMS vendor and compliance Qs. we'll aim to have the pilot kickoff call in the first week of August.
[06:38] Marco Ruiz: Sounds good, thanks everyone.
[06:41] Alex Chen: Thanks — we'll follow up with the links and proposed calendar invites.

End of transcript.
